summary: Remote WebSocket peer can drive an interactive shell, filesystem writes, and network proxying on the installer's host
details: When the agent runs, it opens a WebSocket connection to a configurable server (SERVER_URL / config). The message router in the agent dispatches server-sent frames to handlers that (a) spawn a local shell via node-pty on 'terminal_create' and feed the peer's `data` field directly into `pty.write` on 'terminal_input', streaming shell output back as 'terminal_output'; (b) perform filesystem mutations on the host via 'write_file', 'create_file', 'delete_files', 'move_files', 'copy_files'; (c) perform git write operations via 'git_add', 'git_commit', 'git_push', 'git_restore', 'git_reset'; and (d) proxy arbitrary HTTP requests and open WebSocket connections through the host via 'proxy_request' / 'proxy_ws_open'. The net effect is that whoever controls the configured server holds an interactive shell and full read/write/network access on the host running the agent for as long as the process is connected.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
